details: The US Federal Reserve, under new Chair Kevin Warsh, held interest rates steady at its June 17 meeting but adopted a hawkish tone. Warsh indicated a shift towards less forward guidance, which is expected to increase market reliance on incoming economic data. The updated "dot plot" suggests the potential for a rate hike in 2026, though later projections hint at possible cuts. Additionally, five task forces have been announced to review Fed communications, the inflation framework, the balance sheet, data and methodology, and productivity and jobs.
title: Fed Chair Warsh Signals Hawkish Shift, Less Guidance Post-June Meeting

details: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's latest inflation nowcasting, updated as of June 22, 2026, projects the year-over-year Consumer Price Index (CPI) for June 2026 at 4.01%. The month-over-month Core CPI for June 2026 is estimated to be 0.14%. This follows a month-over-month Core CPI of 0.38% for May 2026. The next official CPI release for June is scheduled for July 14, 2026.
title: US Inflation Nowcasting Projects 4.01% Annual CPI for June
